title: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.isIso_boundedConstructibleBaseChange_of_isProper_padicAlgCl
statement: Let ℓ be a natural number with Fact ℓ.Prime, let k be a field with Fact (ringChar k).Prime and Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ), and let X,Y,X′,Y′ be schemes over Spec k whose structure morphisms are locally of finite type, quasi-compact, and separated. Let f : X ⟶ Y, g : Y′ ⟶ Y, f′ : X′ ⟶ Y′, and g′ : X′ ⟶ X be morphisms over Spec k, and let sq : IsPullback g′ f′ f g. If f is proper, then IsIso (boundedConstructibleBaseChange (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) ℓ k sq.toCommSq), the base-change natural transformation between the bounded constructible pro-étale derived categories with condensed Q̄_ℓ coefficients.

proof.text: Each structure morphism is finite type (locally finite type and quasi-compact). The field spectrum is noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes each corner noetherian, in particular topologically noetherian. For an arbitrary object $K$ of the condensed bounded constructible category on $X$, apply the object clause of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit] to choose a finite intermediate extension $E$ and $K_E\in\mathcal C_E^c(X)$ with an isomorphism $v:T_{E,\Omega}^{X}K_E\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. The categories in this step are condensed module-object categories; no identification with a rationalized integral category is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] to the finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and all four separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Its equivalence $J_X$ gives $M\in\Dbc(X,E)$ and an isomorphism $w:J_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$. This rational category has the same objects as its integral category, so its stated exchange-identification clause applies to $M$. The rational exchange at $M$ is invertible by [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension], since the square is cartesian and $f$ proper. The exchange-identification clause conjugates its image under $J_{Y'}$ to the specified condensed exchange $B_E(J_XM)$. A functor maps an inverse to an inverse, and composition with the comparison isomorphisms preserves invertibility. Naturality at $w$ then gives $B_E(K_E)= (r_{f',E}l_{g',E})(w)\circ B_E(J_XM)\circ ((l_{g,E}r_{f,E})(w))^{-1}$, hence $B_E(K_E)$ is invertible.

proof.text: Use the explicitly stated proper pushforward comparison isomorphisms and exchange equation of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-basechange-compatibility]. It gives $B_\Omega(T_{E,\Omega}^XK_E)=U_{K_E}\circ T_{E,\Omega}^{Y'}(B_E(K_E))\circ S_{K_E}^{-1}$. Step 2 supplies an inverse to the middle factor, and scalar extension maps this inverse to its inverse. Thus this component has inverse $S_{K_E}\circ T_{E,\Omega}^{Y'}(B_E(K_E)^{-1})\circ U_{K_E}^{-1}$. This uses no claim that pushforward comparison is invertible for a nonproper map.

proof.text: Write $F=l_{g,\Omega}r_{f,\Omega}$ and $G=r_{f',\Omega}l_{g',\Omega}$. Naturality at the isomorphism $v$ of Step 1 gives $B_\Omega(K)=G(v)\circ B_\Omega(T_{E,\Omega}^XK_E)\circ F(v)^{-1}$. Its inverse is $F(v)\circ B_\Omega(T_{E,\Omega}^XK_E)^{-1}\circ G(v)^{-1}$, as checked by cancellation. Consequently every component is invertible. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nattrans-isIso-iff-app] to obtain the asserted isomorphism of natural transformations, with exactly the upstream condensed coefficient ring.
